unit.why: A transmitted anecdote about the Maggid of Kozhnitz's childhood: on Hanukkah night his candle miraculously burned all night, his father beat him, and he stayed silent. It is followed by biographical notes on his studies, marriage and later kindness to a benefactor's son-in-law.

stories.start_quote: עוד במכתב הנ"ל וז"ל וכ׳ אלי
stories.end_quote: ה׳ ר״ט לכל שבוע כל ימי חייו
stories.summary_en: As a seven-year-old, the future Maggid of Kozhnitz promised his father to study only as long as a small candle lasted, but angels made it burn all night. Beaten by his father for supposedly playing cards, he would not exploit the honour of Torah to excuse himself. Later he married in Przysucha, was supported by Issachar Berish, and in turn supported Berish's impoverished son-in-law for life.
